newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes a shade down, volumes heavy.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes a shade down, volumes heavy.

text.p: Bullion prices in Hong Kong barely moved, disguising healthy volumes of buying and selling before the market ended a shade below Friday's New York close, gold dealers and traders said on Monday.
"I think the interbank people and professionals are bearish and they've come up against physical buying," said Swiss Bank Corp.'s Anderson Cheung.
Professionals were selling as they established fresh short positions, Cheung said.
"You've got bullish and bearish sentiment, resulting in two-way trade and volumes today were quite substantial," said another bullion trader at an international bank.
The market saw selling interest from producers at around $381.50 per ounce, and buying interest from funds at about $379 per ounce, gold traders said.
Bullion ended at US$380.00/50 an ounce Monday against the gold close on Saturday at US$380.10/60 and New York's US$380.05/55 close on Friday.
Hong Kong gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,503 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from -5.00 at its previous fix. BULLION -
